paper_metadata.title: Credit Default Prediction with Projected Quantum Feature Models and Ensembles

experiments.description: Preliminary simulator study of a hybrid projected-quantum-feature pipeline using a Heisenberg feature map and XGBoost on balanced credit-default subsamples, evaluated first on a statevector simulator and then on an MPS simulator across several qubit/feature sizes.

algorithm.variant: Projected Quantum Features with Heisenberg feature map + XGBoost classifier

hyperparameters.random_seeds: different random seeds used in grid search / validation

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Haar-random single-qubit states in the feature map; hyperparameters selected by grid search over alpha and XGBoost learning rate

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical credit-default features are scaled to [0.3, 0.8], optionally shuffled, then encoded into a Heisenberg feature map circuit; projective measurements are converted into classical projected quantum features for XGBoost.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of whether a customer defaults on balance in the next 18 months.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: One-dimensional Heisenberg interaction terms Hj(xij) = xij (XjXj+1 + YjYj+1 + ZjZj+1)

problem_instance.description: Credit card default prediction on balanced subsamples of the public AmEx default prediction dataset.

dataset_specification.description: Public Kaggle competition dataset; anonymized monthly customer records with delinquency, spending, payment, balance, and risk indicators. Balanced subsamples were used; one experiment used 1,000 samples, with train/test split implied as equal-sized training and test sets in the paper's methodology.

data_preprocessing_details: selected important features using Random Forest
randomly permuted feature order with ShuffleFeatures
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Five-fold cross-validation; test accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and AUC reported for simulator studies.

classical_postprocessing: projective measurement outcomes used as classical features

speedup_claims.caveats: Quantum model accuracy was close to but below the classical baseline in the reported simulator experiments; no runtime speedup was reported.

experiments.description: Quantum hardware evaluation of the same Heisenberg projected-quantum-feature pipeline on balanced credit-default subsamples, first on ibm_brisbane and then on ibm_torino and ibm_marrakesh.

algorithm.variant: Projected Quantum Features with Heisenberg feature map + XGBoost classifier on IBM hardware
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Haar-random single-qubit states; hyperparameters selected by grid search / tuning

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Balanced credit-default features encoded into a Heisenberg feature map; projective measurements converted to classical features for XGBoost.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of customer default in the next 18 months.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: One-dimensional Heisenberg interaction terms Hj(xij) = xij (XjXj+1 + YjYj+1 + ZjZj+1)

problem_instance.description: Balanced subsamples of the public AmEx default prediction dataset evaluated on IBM quantum hardware.

dataset_specification.description: Public Kaggle competition dataset; balanced subsamples used for hardware experiments. One set used 81 qubits / 160 features / 1,000 samples on ibm_brisbane; another used 101 qubits / 174 features / 1,000 samples on ibm_torino; later 101 qubits / 174 features / 500 samples on ibm_marrakesh.

data_preprocessing_details: selected important features using Random Forest
randomly permuted feature order with ShuffleFeatures
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Test accuracy compared against classical baseline; balanced data used for fair comparison.

noise_model.mitigation_details: Random X gates applied before measurement and inverted in post-processing; readout error characterized using target circuit and empty |0...0> circuit.
noise_model.transpilation_target: IBM hardware coupling map and native basis gates
classical_postprocessing: projective measurement outcomes used as classical features

speedup_claims.conditions: balanced hardware experiments on IBM devices
speedup_claims.caveats: Quantum accuracy was slightly below classical accuracy in all reported hardware runs; no runtime or asymptotic speedup was claimed.

experiments.description: Scalability study on balanced data varying the number of qubits while keeping 30 features fixed, using the Heisenberg projected-quantum-feature pipeline and XGBoost on simulator backends.

algorithm.variant: Projected Quantum Features with Heisenberg feature map + XGBoost classifier, qubit-scaling study
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Haar-random single-qubit states; alpha and learning rate selected per qubit count

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 30 selected credit-default features encoded into a Heisenberg feature map; projected measurements fed to XGBoost.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: One-dimensional Heisenberg interaction terms Hj(xij) = xij (XjXj+1 + YjYj+1 + ZjZj+1)

problem_instance.description: Balanced sample of 1,000 instances from the public credit-default dataset used to study performance as qubit count increases.

dataset_specification.description: Balanced subsample of 1,000 records; 30 features retained for the qubit-scaling experiment.

data_preprocessing_details: selected important features using Random Forest
randomly permuted feature order with ShuffleFeatures
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Test-set evaluation with accuracy, precision, recall, F1, and AUC reported.

classical_postprocessing: projective measurement outcomes used as classical features

speedup_claims.conditions: simulator scaling study with fixed 30 features
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports accuracy/AUC across qubit counts but does not claim computational speedup.

experiments.description: Unbalanced-data ensemble study combining classical and quantum projected-quantum-feature models, comparing mean-based ensembles and logistic-regression meta-models on simulator and IBM hardware.

algorithm.variant: Ensemble of classical XGBoost and quantum projected-quantum-feature XGBoost models
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Bayesian optimization with 15 random seeds for classical and quantum XGBClassifier hyperparameters; ensemble built from prediction probabilities.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Credit-default features are scaled, shuffled, encoded with a Heisenberg feature map, measured, and passed to XGBoost; ensemble uses predicted probabilities from classical and quantum models.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of default risk using the CDR metric.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: One-dimensional Heisenberg interaction terms Hj(xij) = xij (XjXj+1 + YjYj+1 + ZjZj+1)

problem_instance.description: Unbalanced 10,000-sample subset of the public credit-default dataset, used for ensemble evaluation with CDR metric.

dataset_specification.description: Unbalanced subsample with approximately 80% negatives and 20% positives, intended to resemble the full dataset distribution; evaluated on MPS simulator and ibm_marrakesh.

data_preprocessing_details: selected important features using Random Forest
randomly permuted feature order with ShuffleFeatures
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: CDR metric reported as mean ± standard deviation across multiple runs/seeds; 225 classical-quantum model combinations evaluated.

noise_model.mitigation_details: Readout-error mitigation via random X twirling and classical inversion; target and empty-circuit sampling used for calibration.
noise_model.transpilation_target: IBM hardware coupling map and native basis gates
classical_postprocessing: mean of classical and quantum prediction probabilities
logistic regression on classical and quantum prediction probabilities

speedup_claims.conditions: unbalanced 10,000-sample evaluation; simulator and IBM hardware
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports modest CDR improvements from ensembles, but no computational speedup or asymptotic advantage.
